content_voiceover: This slide compares three classic myelofibrosis risk stratification tools, IPSS, DIPSS, and DIPSS plus, which build on each other in a testable, layered way. IPSS, the International Prognostic Scoring System, uses five variables at diagnosis, hemoglobin under ten, WBC over twenty five thousand, age over sixty five, constitutional symptoms, and peripheral blood blasts one percent or more, each worth one point. DIPSS, the dynamic version usable at any time point during follow up, uses the same five variables but doubles the weight of hemoglobin under ten to two points, reflecting its outsized prognostic impact. DIPSS plus builds further on DIPSS by adding three more variables, unfavorable karyotype, transfusion dependency, and platelet count under one hundred thousand, each worth one point. Risk groups are defined by total score, and remember the cutoffs shift between systems, for IPSS and DIPSS plus, low is zero, intermediate one is one, intermediate two is two to three, and high is three or more for IPSS, four or more for DIPSS plus. For DIPSS specifically, because hemoglobin is worth two points, the ranges differ, intermediate one is a score of one to two, intermediate two is three to four, and high is five to six. Median survival drops sharply across risk groups, roughly one hundred thirty five months in low risk IPSS down to just twenty seven months in high risk, with DIPSS and DIPSS plus showing similarly steep declines, sixteen months median survival in DIPSS plus high risk.
keypoints: IPSS uses five variables, each worth one point, hemoglobin, WBC, age, constitutional symptoms, and blasts
DIPSS uses the same five variables but doubles hemoglobin under ten to two points
DIPSS plus adds karyotype, transfusion dependency, and platelet count under one hundred thousand as three more one point variables
Risk group cutoffs differ between IPSS, DIPSS, and DIPSS plus scoring scales
High risk median survival ranges roughly sixteen to twenty seven months across the three systems
keypoint_voiceover: Track the progression across these three scores, IPSS gives the baseline five clinical variables, DIPSS reweights hemoglobin to reflect its stronger prognostic pull and works at any timepoint, and DIPSS plus layers on cytogenetics, transfusion need, and thrombocytopenia for the most refined risk estimate, with high risk median survival dropping to around sixteen months.
